title: Answer
description:
This priest-king bears two titles. He brings bread and wine, he blesses, and he receives a tenth from the patriarch.

He is shown without father, mother, genealogy, beginning of days, or end of life. That does not deny that he lived. It is the portrait the text itself gives.

He resembles the Son in the way the office is presented, not by a claim about his flesh. As the text presents him, he remains a priest continually.

The later priestly tribe paid that tenth in the patriarch. His tenth outranks the tenths that tribe later collected. Their claim already stands beneath this priest.
